title: Lemon Garlic Chicken Tray Bake
seoTitle: Lemon Garlic Chicken Tray Bake | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Bright citrus thighs with roasted broccoli and baby potatoes for eight
subtitle: Bright citrus thighs with roasted broccoli and baby potatoes for eight
description: Bone-in chicken thighs roast on a half-sheet with lemon, garlic, broccoli, and halved baby potatoes. The pan juices become a simple finishing sauce at the line.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Lemon Garlic Chicken Tray Bake in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Heat oven and prep pans
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 425°F. Line two half-sheet pans with parchment. Pat chicken dry so skin crisps instead of steaming in the oven. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Build the lemon garlic marinade
steps.instruction: Whisk olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, minced garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper until emulsified and fragrant. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Season chicken and vegetables
steps.instruction: Toss thighs with half the marinade until coated. Toss potatoes and broccoli with remaining marinade until glossy and evenly seasoned.

steps.title: Roast until chicken is done
steps.instruction: Arrange thighs skin-side up with potatoes around edges and broccoli in gaps. Roast 32–38 minutes until internal temp hits 165°F and skin is golden.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Lemon Garlic Chicken Tray Bake onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Rest and serve from the tray
steps.instruction: Rest pans 5 minutes. Spoon pan juices over portions at the line. Chicken should feel firm with clear juices, not pink at the bone.

proTips: Dry thighs thoroughly—wet skin never crisps on a crowded hall tray.
Rotate pans top to bottom halfway for even browning in a busy oven.
Add lemon slices only for the last 10 minutes so they caramelize, not burn.
tonightSpread: Warm whole-wheat pita with tzatziki for scooping pan juices.
Simple arugula salad with shaved parmesan and lemon vinaigrette.
leftovers: Shred leftover thighs into a next-day grain bowl with cucumber and feta.
Chop roasted potatoes into a breakfast hash with scrambled eggs.
whyCrewsLikeIt: High-protein comfort without heavy cream. Everything finishes on one tray, portions fast, and reheats cleanly on the next shift.
mealPrepNotes: Marinate thighs up to 24 hours. Chop veg the night before in labeled bins. Hold finished trays at 170°F up to 90 minutes. Station: Split two half-sheet pans so thighs char instead of steam across eight portions. Station: Rest trays 5 minutes before portioning so juices redistribute into the meat. Station: Line a sheet pan with foil under the serving tray for fast post-meal cleanup.
substitutions: Swap broccoli for green beans or asparagus in season.
